title: Introduce prefetch-policer and quant-fallback conductor
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a tenant-facing prefetch policer and runtime conductor that coordinates quantized fallbacks; includes CLI tooling to validate cost-manifests and a small unit-econ smoke harness.
description:
Motivation: Some tenants observed large cost spikes from naive prefill decisions during bursty traffic. This PR introduces a prefetch policer that applies conservative token-prefill allowances per-tenant and a quant-fallback conductor that orchestrates safe transitions to lower-precision model variants when capacity or unit economics dictate. The goal is predictable unit economics while preserving latency SLOs where possible.

What this PR does (high level): 1) prefetch policer: a light-weight admission controller that consumes tenant budget profiles and recent warm-start telemetry to allow/deny or rate-limit prefill requests; supports soft/hard quotas and graceful degrade policies. 2) quant-fallback conductor: runtime coordinator that executes a 3-step safe transition (probe -> audition -> promote) to quantized model variants; performs output-sanity checks and automatic rollback when eval metrics degrade. 3) CLI: cost-manifest validator and dry-run simulator for tenant teams to preview how policies would apply to historical traces. 4) unit-econ smoke harness: small integration test that runs sampled traces in CI to detect large per-token cost regressions when policies are active.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in issue ENG-3912 - [x] Implementation of policer and conductor services - [x] Runtime hooks for model routing and cache-key tagging - [x] End-to-end tests for safe rollback behavior - [x] CLI docs and examples - [x] Telemetry: new metrics and traces instrumented

Commits summary: - Add prefetch policer service, admission API and in-memory policy store - Introduce quant-fallback conductor and state machine for safe transitions - Add policy CLI: validate / dry-run / export - Telemetry: prefill.allow/deny counters, quant.fallback.attempt/success/fail metrics - Tests: e2e smoke harness and unit tests for policy edge cases - Docs: CLI usage and operational runbook

Files changed (high level): - services/prefill/policer.go (new) - services/conductor/quant_fallback.go (new) - cli/cost-manifest/validate.go (new) - telemetry/metrics_registry.go (minor additions) - serving/router.go (hook points for policer/conductor) - integration/tests/prefill_smoke_test.go (new) - docs/ops/prefetch-policer.md (new)

CI and validation: CI run showed one flaky test initially (integration/prefill_smoke_test) due to nondeterministic synthetic traces; fixed by seeding generator and adding a retry on transient network binds. Full pipeline now passes (unit, integration, lint). Performance bench: small overhead (p50 +2ms) on cold starts when policer evaluates; typical steady-state shows no measurable latency regression thanks to async evaluation and cached policy decisions.

Review conversation snapshot: Marco Rivera: "Nice separation between admission control and fallback orchestration; can you add a circuit-breaker metric for the conductor to detect thrash?" Aisha Patel (author): "Added quant.fallback.circuit_open_count and test coverage; added note to runbook for knob overrides." Lina Zhang: "Concern: how does this interact with tenant Dedicated pools?" Aisha: "Policer consults tenant capacity hints; for Dedicated SKUs we default to permissive mode and only apply soft-prefetch caps unless explicitly configured." Tomás Ortega: "CLI is useful — add an example mapping a trace to policy output." Aisha: "Added three example traces and an explanatory section in docs. "

Operational notes and runbook highlights: - Default policy is permissive for enterprise Dedicated customers; strict for self-serve tenants with >10% warmup cost variance. - Safe-mode: when conductor sees >2 consecutive quant audition failures it opens circuit for 30 minutes and annotates traces. - Telemetry to watch: prefill.deny_rate, quant.fallback.success_rate, quant.fallback.rollback_rate, unit_econ.delta_cost_pct. - Suggested alert: quant.fallback.rollback_rate > 5% over 15m triggers on-call.

Merge details: squashed merge. Post-merge: deployed to staging with feature flag prefetch_policer.enabled=false by default; slowly enabled for two pilot tenants during the rollout window. No incident during rollout; pilot tenants reported 8-12% reduction in prefill-related token spend for bursty traces.

Follow-ups: - ENG-4110: policy-as-code export/import across tenants (separate PR) - Add long-term storage for policy decisions for offline auditing - Add adaptive thresholds based on observed unit econ deltas (research spike planned)
